# Command-line tools

## Visualizer: `python -m celery_viz`

The monitor itself. In the demo stack the `viz` service runs it with the flags shown in [services](services.md).

```text
usage: celery_viz [-h] [--broker BROKER] [--replay REPLAY] [--speed SPEED] [--host HOST]
                  [--port PORT] [--hung-after HUNG_AFTER] [--lost-after LOST_AFTER]
                  [--drain-grace DRAIN_GRACE] [--queue-metrics-url QUEUE_METRICS_URL]
                  [--catalog CATALOG] [--ui-dir UI_DIR] [--ignore-task NAME] [--max-runs MAX_RUNS]
                  [--keep-args] [--keep-result]

Read-only Celery workflow visualizer.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --broker BROKER       broker URL of the Celery deployment to observe
  --replay REPLAY       replay a recorded events file (one JSON object per line) instead of
                        connecting
  --speed SPEED         replay speed multiplier
  --host HOST           bind address; the API has no auth, keep it on loopback unless proxied
  --port PORT
  --hung-after HUNG_AFTER
                        flag tasks running longer than this many seconds as suspected hung
  --lost-after LOST_AFTER
                        never call a worker lost before this many seconds of silence (it is also
                        at least 3x the worker's own heartbeat period)
  --drain-grace DRAIN_GRACE
                        how long a worker that announced shutdown may keep running tasks before
                        they count as lost (match your orchestrator's stop grace period)
  --queue-metrics-url QUEUE_METRICS_URL
                        RabbitMQ Prometheus endpoint for measured ready/unacked, e.g.
                        http://rabbitmq:15692/metrics/detailed?family=queue_coarse_metrics
  --catalog CATALOG     enable launching: 'package.module:object' providing describe()/launch().
                        Off by default (read-only)
  --ui-dir UI_DIR       directory with the built UI (default: celery_viz/ui_dist when present)
  --ignore-task NAME    drop this task name entirely (repeatable), e.g. a periodic sweep that
                        would flood the run list
  --max-runs MAX_RUNS
  --keep-args           keep task args/kwargs (default: dropped; may contain personal data)
  --keep-result         keep task results (default: dropped)
```

## Spot-eviction simulator: `python3 app/chaos/spot_killer.py`

Runs on the host and shells out to `docker`. Used by `make test-spot`.

```text
usage: spot_killer.py [-h] [--api API] [--chunks CHUNKS]
                      [--mode {sigkill,term-kill,sigterm,child}] [--kill-at KILL_AT]
                      [--grace GRACE] [--replace-after REPLACE_AFTER]
                      [--stall-timeout STALL_TIMEOUT] [--wait-for-police WAIT_FOR_POLICE]
                      [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--pause]

Spot Instance chaos simulator.

Starts a call, waits until about half the chunks are done and one is mid-flight, then "evicts" the
worker running it, boots a replacement, and reports what happened to the in-flight chunk.

Runs on your HOST (standard library only, shells out to `docker`). From the repo root:

    python3 app/chaos/spot_killer.py                    # SIGKILL: the instance vanishes
    python3 app/chaos/spot_killer.py --mode term-kill   # SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a short grace period
    python3 app/chaos/spot_killer.py --mode sigterm     # warm shutdown only (NOT data loss; see below)
    python3 app/chaos/spot_killer.py --mode child       # kill only the pool child (an OOM-kill)
    python3 app/chaos/spot_killer.py --pause            # narrate and wait for Enter at each step

Kill modes and what they teach:
  sigkill    Whole container dies instantly, AMQP connection drops. With acks_late RabbitMQ requeues the
             unacked message. With Celery's defaults the message was already ACKed: the chunk is gone.
  term-kill  What a real Spot eviction looks like: a notice (SIGTERM), a short window, then power-off.
  sigterm    Celery treats SIGTERM as a *warm shutdown*: stop taking work, finish what is running, exit.
             The in-flight chunk completes. Great graceful behaviour, but not an eviction.
  child      Only the pool child process dies; the parent worker lives on and keeps its broker
             connection, so RabbitMQ never notices. This is what task_reject_on_worker_lost is for.

Exit code: 0 = call completed on its own, 2 = completed only because the Task Police intervened,
1 = call failed or never finished.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --api API
  --chunks CHUNKS
  --mode {sigkill,term-kill,sigterm,child}
  --kill-at KILL_AT     fraction of chunks that must be done before the kill
  --grace GRACE         term-kill: seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL
  --replace-after REPLACE_AFTER
                        seconds before the replacement worker boots
  --stall-timeout STALL_TIMEOUT
                        declare the call STUCK after this long without any change
  --wait-for-police WAIT_FOR_POLICE
                        after a stall, keep waiting this long for the Task Police
  --timeout TIMEOUT
  --pause               wait for Enter before each step
```

## Prefetch experiment: `python3 app/chaos/prefetch_demo.py`

Used by `make test-prefetch`.

```text
usage: prefetch_demo.py [-h] [--api API] [--rabbitmq RABBITMQ] [--chunks CHUNKS] [--slow SLOW]

Show what worker_prefetch_multiplier does to fairness. No failures involved.

Runs a call where two of the chunks are very slow, samples RabbitMQ's view of the heavy_processing
queue every second (ready vs unacked messages, per-consumer prefetch_count), and prints which worker
ran which chunk plus how long each worker sat idle.

With multiplier 4 each worker *reserves* 4 messages up front. A worker stuck on a slow chunk keeps
the ones queued behind it hostage while its neighbour finishes everything else and goes idle.
With multiplier 1 a worker only holds what it is running, so work flows to whoever is free.

Standard library only; run from the repo root (normally via `make test-prefetch`).

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --api API
  --rabbitmq RABBITMQ
  --chunks CHUNKS
  --slow SLOW          comma-separated chunk indexes that take ~22s
```

## Ground-truth check: `python3 scripts/check_viz.py`

Used by `make viz-check`.

```text
usage: check_viz.py [-h] [--api API] [--viz VIZ] [--calls CALLS] [--chunks CHUNKS]
                    [--timeout TIMEOUT]

Validate the live visualizer against ground truth (the pipeline's own database).

Submits N calls, waits for them to finish, then checks that the monitor (celery_viz) shows the same
outcome for every run and every chunk. Run it after any change to the collector or reducer:

    python3 scripts/check_viz.py            # 15 calls x 3 chunks, about 3 minutes
    python3 scripts/check_viz.py --calls 4 --chunks 2

Exit code 0 only if the monitor agrees with the database on every run. Standard library only.

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --api API
  --viz VIZ
  --calls CALLS
  --chunks CHUNKS
  --timeout TIMEOUT
```
